Cross-Platform Builds > Cross-Compiling for ARM and macOS

Cross-Compiling for ARM and macOS

The ARM and macOS targets do not need a separately prepared toolchain: stock Zig 0.17.0 ships the required libc (musl/glibc/darwin), so you can cross-compile directly on a Linux x86_64 host. This differs from FreeBSD (see the FreeBSD Cross-Compilation page).

Before you start

  • Work from the sci repository root; build.zig and the runtime sources are resolved relative to it.
  • Use a fresh install prefix such as -p zig-out-arm or -p zig-out-mac-arm; never cross-build into the default zig-out/, because the std-runtime test expects the native prefix to exist.
  • -Dllvm=false is required for these cross targets: stock Zig ships the target libc, but not a cross LLVM-C backend. Skipped llvmc tests are expected.

Three-point verification checklist

  1. Identify: file <prefix>/bin/sa must match the intended target (ARM aarch64 ELF, or Mach-O arm64 / x86_64).
  2. Load: on the target machine (or under qemu-aarch64 / qemu-x86_64), run ./sa --version; a wrong interpreter or missing dynamic loader fails here with No such file or directory.
  3. Behave: run at least one sa build-exe of a hello program on the target. Link-only success does not exercise the networking/errno paths called out in the note below.
# ARM Linux under QEMU on the build host
qemu-aarch64 -L /usr/aarch64-linux-gnu ./zig-out-arm/bin/sa --version
qemu-aarch64 -L /usr/aarch64-linux-gnu ./zig-out-arm/bin/sa build-exe hello.sa -o hello_arm
file hello_arm    # ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM aarch64

The -L path must point at the target sysroot that matches the triple; using the host's /lib here produces misleading loader errors.

ARM Linux (aarch64)

# 运行目录：sci 仓库根目录
zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-linux-gnu -Dllvm=false -p zig-out-arm
file zig-out-arm/bin/sa
# 期望：ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM aarch64, ... interpreter /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1

macOS (ARM / Intel)

# 运行目录：sci 仓库根目录
zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-macos -Dllvm=false -p zig-out-mac-arm
zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-macos -Dllvm=false -p zig-out-mac-x64
file zig-out-mac-arm/bin/sa
# 期望：Mach-O 64-bit arm64 executable

Products include sa, hubproxy, libsa_asm.a, libsa_std.a, and libsa_std.dylib.

Interpreting failures

MessageMeaning
undefined symbol: _c_recvmsgan extern "c" declaration used a name that does not exist in the target libc; macOS dylib linking is strict, so this fails there while ELF tolerated it
No such file or directory when executing the cross-built binarythe target interpreter/dynamic loader is absent; install the target sysroot or pass it to QEMU with -L
llvmc tests skippednormal with -Dllvm=false

Known Fix: the recvmsg Symbol Name

portableRecvmsg in src/runtime/sa_std.zig once declared the libc function as extern "c" fn c_recvmsg — that symbol does not exist at all. Linux could link because ELF shared libraries allow undefined symbols, while a macOS dylib rejects them by default (undefined symbol: _c_recvmsg). It has been fixed to the real symbol name recvmsg. Lesson: when adding an extern declaration, the name must match the target libc's actual symbol character for character, and it should be verified on macOS (strict dylib linking).

NoteOn macOS, the recvmsg semantics, the __error() errno path, and the msghdr layout have not yet been test-run on real hardware; cross-compilation currently guarantees only that linking passes.
